summary.title: Let's Build a Regex Engine
summary.one_liner: You learn how a regex engine works internally by building one in four stages: grammar, parser, compiler to finite automaton, and matcher.
keywords: how regex works under the hood
takeaways: Regex patterns are parsed into an abstract syntax tree using parser combinators.
A regex is compiled into a finite state automaton representation.
Two matchers are covered: a backtracking matcher (similar to .NET) and a linear-time matcher (similar to RE2).
Understanding grammars and languages helps in designing the regex parser.
A complete implementation is available on GitHub.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to a multi-part series on implementing a feature-rich regex engine. It explains why building one is a good learning exercise, since it touches parsers, compilers, automata, graphs, and trees. The series is split into four parts: grammar, parser (parser combinators producing an AST), compiler (finite state automaton), and matcher (backtracking and linear-time algorithms). The author aims for performance comparable to NSRegularExpression, which uses the ICU regex engine, and says basic regex knowledge is assumed.
